title: Introduction to CS Fundamentals (Hardware)
summary: Two sessions for the OLIVE-LEARN programme, tracing a running program from the instruction pipeline down to the logic gates that execute it.
points: Part 1 — Efficient code execution: CPU instruction pipelining, the memory hierarchy and caching, and how DMA, the NIC and the APU move work off the core.
Part 2 — Circuit-level computation: built up from SR and D latches to a 4-bit register, 1-bit and 4-bit adders, and an arithmetic logic unit.

title: Assembly Programming Workshop
summary: Low-level programming taught from the hardware upward, with every slide, exercise and solution published as a public repository.
points: Hardware groundwork: chipsets, buses, and the path an instruction takes to reach the CPU.
ARM assembly: definitions, the core instruction set and worked examples, followed by guided exercises.
Each exercise solved twice — once in ARM assembly, once in Python — so the cost of an abstraction was visible side by side.
Extension material: a Breakout game implemented in x86 assembly alongside C and C++ versions, for participants continuing on their own.

title: Introduction to Competitive Programming
summary: An entry point into contest-style problem solving, aimed at students with working code but no method for choosing an approach.
points: Complexity analysis first: reading a problem’s constraints to rule out approaches before writing any code.
The core data structures and the recurring algorithm patterns that most contest problems reduce to.

title: Introduction to Python
summary: A beginner track taught through two builds rather than through syntax slides.
points: A console tic-tac-toe game: representing board state, validating input and detecting a win.
A short data exercise: reading a CSV file and plotting it as charts.
